parts.text: A student measures the resistance of a light‑emitting diode (LED) when the current in it changes. The student sets up the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student: • connects a voltmeter to measure the potential difference across the 220 Ω resistor • closes the switch • records the voltmeter reading V PQ in the top row of Table 2.1 • opens the switch.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 2.1, draw the symbol for a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference across the 220 Ω resistor. [2]

ms.label: 2(a)(i)
ms.text:
correct voltmeter symbol
voltmeter in parallel with the 220 Ω resistor

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The voltmeter reading is shown in Fig. 2.2. Fig. 2.2 Write down the reading in the top row of Table 2.1 under the heading V PQ . [1] Table 2.1 resistance between P and Q / Ω V PQ / V V QR / V I / A R LED / Ω 220 2.1 330 2.0 0.0076 263

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student: • disconnects the voltmeter from points P and Q • reconnects the voltmeter across the LED between points Q and R • closes the switch. • records the voltmeter reading V QR in the top row of Table 2.1 • opens the switch. Calculate the current I in the circuit in part (a) using the equation I = V PQ R where R = 220 Ω. Record your answer in the top row of Table 2.1. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Calculate the resistance R LED of the LED using the equation R LED = V QR I Record your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment in the top row of Table 2.1. [2]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
190 / 191 / 192 / 193 Ω or values rounding to these
answer expressed to 2/3 significant figures

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student: • removes the 220 Ω resistor from the circuit and replaces it with a 330 Ω resistor • reconnects the voltmeter across the resistor between points P and Q • repeats parts (a) to (c) for the 330 Ω resistor. Use the information in Table 2.1 to calculate the value of the potential difference V PQ across the 330 Ω resistor. Show your working and record your answer in Table 2.1. [1]
